To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the radiation induced defects in the CMOS devices are the interface states and oxide charges and the radiation induced defects of the bipolar device are the interface states, oxide charges and trapped charges.

the x-ray radiation damage in bipolar and CMOS devices can be divided into two categories: (1) interface states, positive charges and neutral traps induced damage and (2) oxide trapped charges and oxide defects induced damage.

x-ray induced damage is not a major concern for high performance self-aligned, double-polysilicon bipolar transistors and that the radiation induced defects can degrade the performance of CMOS DRAM circuits.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the radiation induced degradation of high performance self aligned bipolar devices and deep-submicron CMOS devices.
the radiation effects of x-rays on CMOS and bipolar device performance and reliability.
radiation damage in semiconductor devices and the impact of this damage on the reliability of integrated circuits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of x-ray lithography on CMOS and self-aligned bipolar transistors is a serious concern for the fabrication of VLSI circuits.
the x-ray radiation induced damage is detrimental to the device performance and reliability of high performance bipolar and CMOS devices.
x-ray radiation induced damage in bipolar devices can be controlled by proper design and processing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the radiation induced damage is the dominant mechanism for the degradation of bipolar device current gain.

the hot-carrier properties in x-ray damaged devices are similar to those in the electron irradiated devices, and the x-ray radiation induced damage in CMOs devices is more severe than that in the bipolar devices.
x-rays can induce radiation damage in CMOs and bipolar devices, which can cause the degradation in the device performance, and the reliability of the circuits.
The main takeaway from our work is that
x-ray lithography can be used to fabricate high performance devices without any radiation induced performance degradation.
the radiation induced damage in the bipolar devices is mainly due to the x-ray induced oxide defects and interface states.
the x-ray radiation source used in x-ray lithography does not degrade the performance or the long term reliability of the self-aligned, high performance bipolar device.
